prompt: Order the steps of a typical CI/CD pipeline after a developer merges code.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: The build is deployed to staging
Code is merged into the main branch
After approval, it is deployed to production

task.explanation: Merge triggers the build, tests gate the build, staging is checked, then production.

prompt: Order the steps for releasing a new version of a client's iOS app.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: Prepare release notes and store screenshots
Finish QA and client UAT on a TestFlight build
Submit the build for App Store review

task.explanation: Test, prepare store assets, submit, wait for approval, release, then monitor.

prompt: Mark the problems in this go-live plan for a web platform.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: Deploy at 10:00 Tuesday when the whole team is online.
Back up the database before the deploy.
No rollback plan needed, we tested it on staging.
segments.issue: Staging cannot catch everything; always know how to roll back.

segments.text: Smoke test login, search and checkout right after deploy.
Tell the client after the release is live, if it goes well.
segments.issue: The client should know the release time in advance and be told the outcome either way.

segments.text: Watch error monitoring for two hours after release.

prompt: A web app's release log is shown. Work out the change failure rate and the average time to restore after a failed release.

task.prompt: Calculate each value from the data.
task.explanation: 3 of 20 deployments failed: 3 / 20 = 15%. Restore times 30 + 90 + 60 = 180 minutes over 3 incidents: 60 minutes on average.

prompt: Right after a release, users report they cannot log in. The previous version worked.

task.prompt: Right after a release, users report they cannot log in. The previous version worked.

steps.question: What is usually the quickest safe action?
options: Roll back to the previous version, then investigate
Write a fix live in production
steps.explanation: Rolling back restores service fast; the fix can then be made and tested properly.

steps.question: What do you tell the client?
options: That there was an issue with the release, it is rolled back, and when you will update them
That users are doing it wrong
That it was the hosting provider
steps.explanation: Prompt, factual communication with the next update time keeps trust.

prompt: The client wants a new feature live for a marketing campaign on Monday, but QA is not finished. The team suggests releasing the code behind a feature flag.

task.prompt: The client wants a new feature live for a marketing campaign on Monday, but QA is not finished. The team suggests releasing the code behind a feature flag.

steps.question: What does a feature flag allow?
options: Deploying code with the feature switched off, then turning it on later without a new release
steps.explanation: Flags separate deploying code from releasing a feature to users.

steps.question: What is a sensible plan?
options: Deploy with the flag off, finish QA on production with the flag on for internal users, then switch it on for everyone
Switch it on for all users immediately
Release without the flag and hope
steps.explanation: Flags let you test safely in production and turn the feature on when it is ready.

options: An urgent fix released to production outside the normal release schedule
mcq.explanation: Hotfixes address urgent production problems without waiting for the next planned release.

prompt: Why can't an agency promise the exact day a mobile app update reaches the App Store?

options: Apple's review takes a variable amount of time and can reject builds
mcq.explanation: Store review is outside the agency's control, so plan a buffer and avoid promising the exact day.

prompt: What is the main benefit of a phased (staged) rollout to 10% of users first?

options: Problems affect fewer users and can be caught before everyone gets the update
It removes the need for QA
mcq.explanation: Phased rollouts limit the blast radius of a bad release.
